target_customer: Indian retail investors who hold mutual funds or shares and need cash
problem: Investors either pay personal loan rates above 18 percent or sell investments; Yenmo lets them pledge holdings digitally for a credit line from regulated lenders starting at 9.89 percent.
business_model: Loan service provider earning from partner lenders; loans sanctioned by RBI-regulated lenders (site names Bajaj Finance and DSP); API for other companies

founders.name: Ashutosh Purohit
founders.background_notes: YC page says he and Aryan attended the same college; not named.

founders.name: Aryan Agarwal
previous_startups: A capital management company in India with over 2M dollars AUM (per YC page)

technical_complexity.rationale: Digital KYC, fund pledging via registrars and e-mandate with partner lenders is integration-heavy standard fintech engineering.

defensibility.rationale: The product depends on lender partners and banks, NBFCs and fintechs offer similar loans; no exclusive access found.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Business Standard (2025) reports many fintechs entering secured lending against mutual funds; this is after founding and not a documented takeover.

market_need_then: YC description cites over 30 percent of personal loan borrowers holding investments and paying double the rate they qualify for; regulated banks and NBFCs already offered loans against mutual funds.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain pricing-led messaging: no EMI, no foreclosure charge

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive invented name with press coverage of its funding, but no brand-specific press or community found.

outcome_analysis: Yenmo is an active five person YC W24 lender-marketplace that announced a 500 thousand dollar YC-led round in March 2024 and a later Rs 9.2 crore round led by YC with Pioneer Fund and Zaka VC. No exit or failure was found. Its growth depends on partner lender terms in a market where banks and fintechs compete on the same product.
notes: Stages are other because sources do not label them. The second round is Rs 9.2 crore (INR 92 million); no USD figure or date was stated in the snippet I saw (one aggregator suggests March 2025, unverified), so amount and date are null. Total raised unverified: CB Insights shows 1.56M. Founded year not stated by YC. Dated competitor sources near 2024 not found; later Business Standard coverage names other fintechs.
